defects.description: The worked example mixes mutually inconsistent bases: it says CLP 1,350,000 taxable includes a CLP 150,000 non-taxable allowance; it then adds that allowance as a separate row to CLP 1,500,000 gross. Summing displayed rows gives CLP 1,386,982 while the printed result is CLP 1,236,982, a CLP 150,000 mismatch. The final amount is only consistent if gross already includes the allowance and the +allowance row is not added.

The linked cotizacion-voluntaria-afp-independiente article still says 1.62% is the current SIS rate since April 2026. SP's verified rate changed to 1.78% from August 2026. This contradicts the corrected page and the cluster-level closure claim.

The linked sueldo-imponible-chile article still describes mandatory AFP saving as approximately 10.5% and calculates its example with 10.5%, while stating AFP commission is additional. SP and the current registry separate 10% savings from the commission, so the cluster still contains a false/duplicative deduction description.

The article applies first-time affiliation rules to a person's 'primer empleo formal'. SP defines the relevant group as people entering the mandatory individual capitalization system for the first time; prior independent/voluntary affiliation can make those conditions differ. The current AFP Uno award window is 2025-10-01 through 2027-09-30; the article states its start but omits the end date. The 24-month rule itself is supported for first-time system entrants, and no annual transfer cap is supported.

The linked sueldo-imponible-chile article applies IUSC to gross CLP 1,200,000 without subtracting mandatory AFP, health and worker AFC. Its own listed deductions total CLP 217,200, leaving CLP 982,800 before any AFP fee. Using current 10% saving, 0.6% AFC, 7% health and current AFP fees gives RLI CLP 971,400–983,280 (CLP 971,520 at Capital 1.44%); applying the stated 4% factor to gross therefore overstates tax base by CLP 216,720–228,600 and tax by CLP 8,668.80–9,144.00.

The new summary table labels employee AFC as 0.6% and only excludes house-particular workers, omitting fixed-term workers' 0% share. It also summarizes the employer 30% housing/education loan limit without the statutory condition that the employer pay the instalment directly to the financial institution or education service.
